pr_body:
Motivation:

In this issue(https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11578 ) discussed that tilde should not be encoded in `QueryStringEncoder`, this pr is to fix this problem

Modification:

Modified `QueryStringEncoder` so that it does not encode tilde, and added a test case

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11578
pr_comments: `QueryStringDecoder` has already done this, I added a test case to verify this

issue_context.title: QueryStringEncoder encodes tilde
issue_context.body:
As per [the comment](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/QueryStringEncoder.java#L235-L249) tile is unreserved and doesn't need encoded. But is encoded.

[RFC3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.3)

### Expected behavior
tilde shouldn't be escaped.

### Actual behavior
tilde is escaped

### Steps to reproduce
var encoder = new QueryStringEncoder("https://google.com");
encoder.addParam("test", "a~b");

### Netty version
4.1
comments: Sounds good, Would you like to provide a PR?

review_comments:
Please also update the javadocs:

```
      unreserved  = ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~"
```
Do I still need to add * in the javadoc?
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.2 Here it says * is reserved. So I guess we need to encode it.

@skyguard1 

After reading more, I'm leaning towards *NOT* encoding an asterisk. Sorry for the confusion, but encoding it or not may not be as straightforward as we thought. 


https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25085992/when-should-an-asterisk-be-encoded-in-an-http-url here it suggests not encoding *. 

From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding#Percent_character
> In the "query" component of a URI (the part after a ? character), for example, / is still considered a reserved character but it normally has no reserved purpose, unless a particular URI scheme says otherwise. The character does not need to be percent-encoded when it has no reserved purpose.

I think it also applies to *.

Considering the adoption of encoding/decoding an asterisk listed in the above StackOverflow post, it shows only PHP rawurlencode() does the work. Java utils and JS utils do not encode. If we choose to encode an asterisk, we are at a risk to break our clients and downstreams.

Can we separate adding `~` to this list and removing `*` from this list?

As mentioned in the original issue, the [spec seems clear](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.3) about not needing to encode `~` so that seem non-contentious.

Let us add `~` to this list in this PR and we can discuss removing `*` in a different PR.
@NiteshKant Sure.According to @zizhong comments, I think it’s better not to encode * now
